what: Hawaii braces for potential first direct hit by a hurricane in 34 years

clean_source_blocks.text: Watch: Strong winds and downpours in Maui and Honolulu as storm Lala approaches Hawaii is bracing for what could be its first direct hit from a hurricane since 1992, as category one storm Lala churns off its coast. Packing 75mph (120km/h) winds, Lala gained hurricane strength on Saturday. In a worst-case scenario, it could dump up to 25in (63cm) of rain on Big Island and produce a 3ft storm surge. A hurricane warning is in effect for Big Island, while Maui County, Oahu, Kauai and Niihau are under a tropical storm warnings. Officials have told residents to prepare for "life-threatening" conditions, including floods and mudslides. The storm is expected to either make landfall or pass close to the southern tip of Big Island on Saturday, before continuing west.

Hawaii braces for tropical cyclone Lala this weekend. This could be the first direct hit that Hawaii has had in nearly 10 years. Largest impacts will be on the big island of Hawaii. MILWAUKEE - The Hawaiian islands are bracing for tropical cyclone Lala this weekend. The National Hurricane Center has issued a hurricane warning for the big island and surrounding waters heading towards the south side of Maui until 6am Sunday, August 16th. A tropical storm watch has been issued for the rest of the Hawaiian islands northwest through Sunday as well.
In a worst-case scenario, category one Lala could dump up to 25in (63cm) of rain on Big Island.

This storm could be significant if it makes landfall on the big island since it would be the first time in nearly 10 years that a hurricane has made landfall there. The last was tropical storm Darby in 2016 and hurricane Iselle in 2014, which both made landfall near the southern side of the island of Hawaii. In 2018, tropical storm Olivia, made landfall on Maui and Lanai. It is rare for a tropical cyclone to make direct landfall on any Hawaiian island since it is such a small place relative to the vast Pacific Ocean. Despite if the eye crosses over lane or not, dangerous winds creating high waves and rip currents, damage to property, storm surge, and flooding will be threats over the weekend.

Myrsky voi rantautua Havaijin saaren eteläosaan tai kulkea sen läheltä ennen jatkamistaan länteen.
Havaijin saarella on hurrikaanivaroitus, ja Mauin piirikunta, Oahu, Kauai ja Niihau ovat trooppiseen myrskyyn liittyvien varoitusten piirissä.
Pahimmillaan sadetta voi kertyä 63 senttimetriä ja myrskyvuoksi nousta noin 0,9 metriin.
Viranomaiset varoittavat hengenvaarallisista tulvista ja maanvyörymistä.
Mauilla ja Honolulussa on koettu voimakkaita tuulia ja rankkasateita Lalan lähestyessä.
National Hurricane Centerin hurrikaanivaroitus koskee Havaijin saarta ja sitä ympäröiviä merialueita kohti Mauin eteläosaa sunnuntaihin 16. elokuuta kello kuuteen saakka.
Muualla Havaijin saaristossa trooppisen myrskyn tarkkailu jatkuu sunnuntaihin asti.
Myrskyn suurimpien vaikutusten odotetaan kohdistuvan Havaijin saareen.

Trooppisten hirmumyrskyjen suora rantautuminen Havaijin saarille on harvinaista.

Watch: Strong winds and downpours in Maui and Honolulu as storm Lala approaches

Hawaii is bracing for what could be its first direct hit from a hurricane since 1992, as category one storm Lala churns off its coast.

Packing 75mph (120km/h) winds, Lala gained hurricane strength on Saturday. In a worst-case scenario, it could dump up to 25in (63cm) of rain on Big Island and produce a 3ft storm surge.

A hurricane warning is in effect for Big Island, while Maui County, Oahu, Kauai and Niihau are under a tropical storm warnings. Officials have told residents to prepare for "life-threatening" conditions, including floods and mudslides.

The storm is expected to either make landfall or pass close to the southern tip of Big Island on Saturday, before continuing west.

The last time a hurricane made landfall on Hawaii's Big Island was 155 years ago, according to the Associated Press news agency.

Over the weekend, Lala will continue moving westwards, and may weaken into a tropical storm, with the centre passing just below Hawaii's other islands.

Hawaii Governor Josh Green warned residents to brace for "an incredible amount of water".

He said on X: "Damaging winds, heavy rain, flash flooding and dangerous surf are possible across the state through the weekend."

At Ellison Onizuka Kona International - Big Island's largest airport - 40% of flights were grounded, according to flightaware.com. Some 80% of flights were called off at its other main airport, Hilo International.

The more dire forecasts from the National Weather Service (NWS) have been issued for areas within Big Island's south-east.

"Major rainfall flooding may prompt many evacuations and rescues," the NWS said, adding that rivers and tributaries "may rapidly overflow their banks in multiple places".

Residents were repeatedly urged by officials to prepare for the storm early.

Local message boards on Facebook show residents filling bags with sand to protect their homes and inquiring whether stores remained open in the early hours on Saturday.

Hawaii County's Civil Defense Agency said public shelters were available in every county on Big Island.

"At this time, you should have completed your storm-ready preparations and focusing on your Sheltering Plan," the agency said on X.

Iniki, a powerful category four storm, was the last hurricane to strike Hawaii back in 1992.

It caused six deaths and $3bn in damage after making landfall on the southern coast of Kauai.

MILWAUKEE - The Hawaiian islands are bracing for tropical cyclone Lala this weekend. The National Hurricane Center has issued a hurricane warning for the big island and surrounding waters heading towards the south side of Maui until 6am Sunday, August 16th. A tropical storm watch has been issued for the rest of the Hawaiian islands northwest through Sunday as well.

Threat to life and property is possible depending on the track, size, and intensity of Lala. Major rainfall may lead to evacuations and rescues, especially on the northeastern side of the island where rain can accumulate to six inches to nearly a foot. Tropical storm Lala is forecast to slowly gain strength to a category-1 hurricane on Saturday prior to potentially making landfall on the big island.

Some recent models have shifted the potential track south, but this cyclone could make landfall in the central to southern portions of Hawaii by Saturday afternoon with sustained winds up to 95mph with gusts over 100mph.

This storm could be significant if it makes landfall on the big island since it would be the first time in nearly 10 years that a hurricane has made landfall there. The last was tropical storm Darby in 2016 and hurricane Iselle in 2014, which both made landfall near the southern side of the island of Hawaii. In 2018, tropical storm Olivia, made landfall on Maui and Lanai.

It is rare for a tropical cyclone to make direct landfall on any Hawaiian island since it is such a small place relative to the vast Pacific Ocean. Despite if the eye crosses over lane or not, dangerous winds creating high waves and rip currents, damage to property, storm surge, and flooding will be threats over the weekend.

This information is provided by the FOX6 Weather Experts, FOX Weather, and the National Hurricane Center

Hawaii residents are scrambling to stock up on food and water, fill their gas tanks and fortify their homes and businesses as Hurricane Lala closes in on the islands.

Lala has strengthened into a Category 1 hurricane and was about 80 miles southeast of South Point in Hawaii County in the latest update, with maximum sustained winds of 75 mph. The storm is moving west toward the Big Island.

Maui County Mayor Richard Bissen urged residents to prepare while they still had time, saying crews across Maui, Molokai and Lanai were also scrambling to get ready.

“Right now we are ready throughout the county: Maui, Molokai, Lanai. We have our personnel ready for working overtime, people you know standby crews, testing all of our generators and just making sure before that any storm comes that we’re ready, so we’re preparing right now,” Bissen told Hawaii News Now.

In flood-prone Kihei, Maui, resident Jon Corbett said his first thought was a notorious stretch of road that has flooded in the past.

“First thing I thought of was the big Kihei road flood in front of Fred’s. They just fixed the road a couple days ago and reopened it. So I’m hoping that handles the storm,” Corbett told News Now.

Across Maui, residents were tying down belongings while businesses boarded up entrances and stacked sandbags, Hawaii News Now reported.

payload.title: Hurrikaani Lala lähestyy Havaijia – sadetta voi tulla jopa 63 senttiä
payload.summary: Ensimmäisen luokan hurrikaaniksi voimistunut Lala voi rantautua Havaijin saaren eteläosaan tai kulkea aivan sen läheltä. Viranomaiset varoittavat tulvista, maanvyörymistä ja vaarallisista rannikko-oloista.
payload.content:
Ensimmäisen luokan hurrikaani Lala lähestyy Havaijia tuulten yltäessä noin 120 kilometriin tunnissa. Lauantaina hurrikaaniksi voimistuneen myrskyn ennustetaan joko rantautuvan Havaijin saaren eteläosaan tai kulkevan aivan sen eteläkärjen läheltä viikonlopun aikana. Viranomaiset kehottavat asukkaita varautumaan hengenvaarallisiin oloihin, sillä rankkasateet voivat synnyttää tulvia ja maanvyörymiä.

## Hurrikaanivaroitus koskee Havaijin saarta

Havaijin saarella on voimassa hurrikaanivaroitus. Mauin piirikunta, Oahu, Kauai ja Niihau ovat trooppiseen myrskyyn liittyvien varoitusten piirissä. National Hurricane Centerin hurrikaanivaroitus koskee Havaijin saarta ja sitä ympäröiviä merialueita kohti Mauin eteläosaa sunnuntaihin 16. elokuuta kello kuuteen saakka. Muualla saaristossa trooppisen myrskyn tarkkailu jatkuu sunnuntaihin asti.

Suurimpien vaikutusten odotetaan kohdistuvan Havaijin saareen. Pahimmassa tapauksessa saarella voi sataa jopa 63 senttimetriä vettä, ja Lala voi nostaa noin 0,9 metrin myrskyvuoksen. Myrsky jatkaa ennusteen mukaan länteen ohitettuaan saaren eteläkärjen tai kuljettuaan sen yli. Vielä ei ole varmaa, ylittääkö myrskyn silmä maa-alueen, mutta vaarallisia vaikutuksia voi esiintyä kummassakin tapauksessa.

## Tulvat ja vaaralliset rannikko-olot uhkana

Vaaraa voi syntyä myös siinä tapauksessa, ettei Lalan silmä kulje saaren yli. Voimakkaat tuulet voivat nostaa korkeita aaltoja ja synnyttää vaarallisia rantavirtauksia, minkä lisäksi uhkina ovat omaisuusvahingot, myrskyvuoksi ja tulvat. Rankkasateiden vuoksi viranomaiset varoittavat erikseen maanvyörymistä. Vaikutusten odotetaan jatkuvan viikonlopun ajan Havaijin saarella ja muualla saaristossa, jossa trooppisen myrskyn oloihin on varauduttu.

Lalan lähestyessä Mauilla ja Honolulussa on jo koettu voimakkaita tuulia ja rankkasateita. Myrskyn suurimpien vaikutusten odotetaan kuitenkin kohdistuvan Havaijin saareen viikonlopun aikana. Muuallakin saaristossa varaudutaan trooppisen myrskyn oloihin, ja varoitukset koskevat useita saaria sekä Havaijin saarta ympäröiviä merialueita.

## Suorat rantautumiset ovat Havaijilla harvinaisia

Trooppisen hirmumyrskyn suora rantautuminen mille tahansa Havaijin saarelle on harvinaista, koska saaret ovat pieniä suhteessa niitä ympäröivään laajaan Tyyneenmereen. Hurrikaani Iselle ja trooppinen myrsky Darby rantautuivat Havaijin saaren eteläosan lähelle vuosina 2014 ja 2016. Trooppinen myrsky Olivia rantautui puolestaan Mauille ja Lanaille vuonna 2018. Tapaukset osoittavat, että suora rantautuminen on mahdollista, vaikka se on saarilla harvinaista.

article.description: Ensimmäisen luokan hurrikaaniksi voimistunut Lala voi rantautua Havaijin saaren eteläosaan tai kulkea aivan sen läheltä. Viranomaiset varoittavat tulvista, maanvyörymistä ja vaarallisista rannikko-oloista.

Watch: Strong winds and downpours in Maui and Honolulu as storm Lala approaches

Hawaii is bracing for what could be its first direct hit from a hurricane since 1992, as category one storm Lala churns off its coast.

Packing 75mph (120km/h) winds, Lala gained hurricane strength on Saturday. In a worst-case scenario, it could dump up to 25in (63cm) of rain on Big Island and produce a 3ft storm surge.

A hurricane warning is in effect for Big Island, while Maui County, Oahu, Kauai and Niihau are under a tropical storm warnings. Officials have told residents to prepare for "life-threatening" conditions, including floods and mudslides.

The storm is expected to either make landfall or pass close to the southern tip of Big Island on Saturday, before continuing west.

The last time a hurricane made landfall on Hawaii's Big Island was 155 years ago, according to the Associated Press news agency.

Over the weekend, Lala will continue moving westwards, and may weaken into a tropical storm, with the centre passing just below Hawaii's other islands.

Hawaii Governor Josh Green warned residents to brace for "an incredible amount of water".

He said on X: "Damaging winds, heavy rain, flash flooding and dangerous surf are possible across the state through the weekend."

At Ellison Onizuka Kona International - Big Island's largest airport - 40% of flights were grounded, according to flightaware.com. Some 80% of flights were called off at its other main airport, Hilo International.

The more dire forecasts from the National Weather Service (NWS) have been issued for areas within Big Island's south-east.

"Major rainfall flooding may prompt many evacuations and rescues," the NWS said, adding that rivers and tributaries "may rapidly overflow their banks in multiple places".

Residents were repeatedly urged by officials to prepare for the storm early.

Local message boards on Facebook show residents filling bags with sand to protect their homes and inquiring whether stores remained open in the early hours on Saturday.

Hawaii County's Civil Defense Agency said public shelters were available in every county on Big Island.

"At this time, you should have completed your storm-ready preparations and focusing on your Sheltering Plan," the agency said on X.

Iniki, a powerful category four storm, was the last hurricane to strike Hawaii back in 1992.

It caused six deaths and $3bn in damage after making landfall on the southern coast of Kauai.

Hawaii braces for tropical cyclone Lala this weekend.

This could be the first direct hit that Hawaii has had in nearly 10 years.

Largest impacts will be on the big island of Hawaii.

MILWAUKEE - The Hawaiian islands are bracing for tropical cyclone Lala this weekend. The National Hurricane Center has issued a hurricane warning for the big island and surrounding waters heading towards the south side of Maui until 6am Sunday, August 16th. A tropical storm watch has been issued for the rest of the Hawaiian islands northwest through Sunday as well.

Threat to life and property is possible depending on the track, size, and intensity of Lala. Major rainfall may lead to evacuations and rescues, especially on the northeastern side of the island where rain can accumulate to six inches to nearly a foot. Tropical storm Lala is forecast to slowly gain strength to a category-1 hurricane on Saturday prior to potentially making landfall on the big island.

Some recent models have shifted the potential track south, but this cyclone could make landfall in the central to southern portions of Hawaii by Saturday afternoon with sustained winds up to 95mph with gusts over 100mph.

This storm could be significant if it makes landfall on the big island since it would be the first time in nearly 10 years that a hurricane has made landfall there. The last was tropical storm Darby in 2016 and hurricane Iselle in 2014, which both made landfall near the southern side of the island of Hawaii. In 2018, tropical storm Olivia, made landfall on Maui and Lanai.

It is rare for a tropical cyclone to make direct landfall on any Hawaiian island since it is such a small place relative to the vast Pacific Ocean. Despite if the eye crosses over lane or not, dangerous winds creating high waves and rip currents, damage to property, storm surge, and flooding will be threats over the weekend.

Maui County Mayor Richard Bissen urged residents to prepare while they still had time, saying crews across Maui, Molokai and Lanai were also scrambling to get ready.

“Right now we are ready throughout the county: Maui, Molokai, Lanai. We have our personnel ready for working overtime, people you know standby crews, testing all of our generators and just making sure before that any storm comes that we’re ready, so we’re preparing right now,” Bissen told Hawaii News Now.

In flood-prone Kihei, Maui, resident Jon Corbett said his first thought was a notorious stretch of road that has flooded in the past.

article.summary: Ensimmäisen luokan hurrikaaniksi voimistunut Lala voi rantautua Havaijin saaren eteläosaan tai kulkea aivan sen läheltä. Viranomaiset varoittavat tulvista, maanvyörymistä ja vaarallisista rannikko-oloista.
article.content:
Ensimmäisen luokan hurrikaani Lala lähestyy Havaijia tuulten yltäessä noin 120 kilometriin tunnissa. Lauantaina hurrikaaniksi voimistuneen myrskyn ennustetaan joko rantautuvan Havaijin saaren eteläosaan tai kulkevan aivan sen eteläkärjen läheltä viikonlopun aikana. Viranomaiset kehottavat asukkaita varautumaan hengenvaarallisiin oloihin, sillä rankkasateet voivat synnyttää tulvia ja maanvyörymiä.

## Hurrikaanivaroitus koskee Havaijin saarta

Havaijin saarella on voimassa hurrikaanivaroitus. Mauin piirikunta, Oahu, Kauai ja Niihau ovat trooppiseen myrskyyn liittyvien varoitusten piirissä. National Hurricane Centerin hurrikaanivaroitus koskee Havaijin saarta ja sitä ympäröiviä merialueita kohti Mauin eteläosaa sunnuntaihin 16. elokuuta kello kuuteen saakka. Muualla saaristossa trooppisen myrskyn tarkkailu jatkuu sunnuntaihin asti.

Suurimpien vaikutusten odotetaan kohdistuvan Havaijin saareen. Pahimmassa tapauksessa saarella voi sataa jopa 63 senttimetriä vettä, ja Lala voi nostaa noin 0,9 metrin myrskyvuoksen. Myrsky jatkaa ennusteen mukaan länteen ohitettuaan saaren eteläkärjen tai kuljettuaan sen yli. Vielä ei ole varmaa, ylittääkö myrskyn silmä maa-alueen, mutta vaarallisia vaikutuksia voi esiintyä kummassakin tapauksessa.

## Tulvat ja vaaralliset rannikko-olot uhkana

Vaaraa voi syntyä myös siinä tapauksessa, ettei Lalan silmä kulje saaren yli. Voimakkaat tuulet voivat nostaa korkeita aaltoja ja synnyttää vaarallisia rantavirtauksia, minkä lisäksi uhkina ovat omaisuusvahingot, myrskyvuoksi ja tulvat. Rankkasateiden vuoksi viranomaiset varoittavat erikseen maanvyörymistä. Vaikutusten odotetaan jatkuvan viikonlopun ajan Havaijin saarella ja muualla saaristossa, jossa trooppisen myrskyn oloihin on varauduttu.

Lalan lähestyessä Mauilla ja Honolulussa on jo koettu voimakkaita tuulia ja rankkasateita. Myrskyn suurimpien vaikutusten odotetaan kuitenkin kohdistuvan Havaijin saareen viikonlopun aikana. Muuallakin saaristossa varaudutaan trooppisen myrskyn oloihin, ja varoitukset koskevat useita saaria sekä Havaijin saarta ympäröiviä merialueita.

## Suorat rantautumiset ovat Havaijilla harvinaisia

Trooppisen hirmumyrskyn suora rantautuminen mille tahansa Havaijin saarelle on harvinaista, koska saaret ovat pieniä suhteessa niitä ympäröivään laajaan Tyyneenmereen. Hurrikaani Iselle ja trooppinen myrsky Darby rantautuivat Havaijin saaren eteläosan lähelle vuosina 2014 ja 2016. Trooppinen myrsky Olivia rantautui puolestaan Mauille ja Lanaille vuonna 2018. Tapaukset osoittavat, että suora rantautuminen on mahdollista, vaikka se on saarilla harvinaista.
